title: Large-scale bioacoustic detection using semantic segmentation: a deep learning framework applied to fin whale calls in ocean-bottom seismometer recordings
abstract: arXiv:2609.13281v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Ocean-bottom seismometers (OBS), originally deployed for geophysical research, continuously record low-frequency sound for months to years across broad areas of ocean, offering a largely untapped resource for passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) of baleen whales. Realising this potential requires automated detection methods that operate reliably across the varied conditions in large sensor networks. We present a deep learning semantic segmentation framework that detects the 20-Hz notes of fin whales (Balaenoptera physalus) in OBS spectrograms, assigning each pixel a probability of belonging to a call and converting the resulting probability maps into time-frequency bounding boxes describing individual detections. translated_title: 基于语义分割的大规模生物声学检测：应用于海底地震仪记录中长须鲸叫声的深度学习框架
translated_abstract: 海底地震仪最初是为地球物理研究而部署的，它们在大范围的海洋区域内连续记录数月至数年的低频声音，为须鲸的被动声学监测（PAM）提供了大量尚未开发的资源。要实现这一潜力，需要能够在大型传感器网络的各种不同条件下可靠运行的自动化检测方法。我们提出了一种深度学习语义分割框架，可以在海底地震仪频谱图中检测长须鲸（Balaenoptera physalus）的20赫兹音符，为每个像素分配其属于一次叫声的概率，并将得到的概率图转换为描述单个检测结果的时间-频率边界框。我们在亚速尔群岛-马德拉-加那利群岛地区一次海底地震仪部署的水听器数据上训练了该模型，然后无需重新训练便将其应用于来自第二个地理位置不同的部署的垂直分量地震仪数据，表
tldr: 该研究提出一种基于深度学习语义分割的框架，能够自动检测海底地震仪记录中长须鲸的20赫兹叫声，并且无需重新训练即可泛化应用于不同地理位置的部署数据。
en_tdlr: This study presents a deep learning semantic segmentation framework that automatically detects fin whale 20-Hz calls in ocean-bottom seismometer recordings, generalizing across geographically distinct deployments without retraining.
